clue.text: Erotic frolicking with European friends with specific interests in common

definitions.text: friends with specific interests in common

indicators.note: frolicking suggests romping about, so the letters of erotic are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something racy going on among a set of continental chums with shared interests.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people sharing tastes or activities.

clue.text: Increases in Conservative branches

parts.note: branches of a tree are limbs

explanation.surface: Talk of growth in the local branches of the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that climbs goes up or rises, as prices do.

clue.text: People accepting offers from sailors around centre of Liskeard

indicators.note: around puts the sailors either side of the central letters

parts.note: tars is an old word for sailors

indicators.note: centre of picks the two central letters of Liskeard

explanation.surface: Sailors in a Cornish town being offered things.
explanation.walkthrough: Liskeard is a Cornish town; its centre is KE.
explanation.definitionFit: Takers are those who accept an offer or bet.

clue.text: For example, the capitalisation in revolutionAry fIsh?

parts.note: a revolutionary is a Red
a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: Pointing out the odd capitals inside the words of the clue itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A and I are a deliberate distraction, so they are themselves an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading clue, which the stray capitals are.

clue.text: Maxes out in tests

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: A student scoring full marks in their tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are examinations, formal tests.

clue.text: Minor injury from bit of egg in pop gun?

indicators.note: in places the egg's bit inside the word for pop

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, DAD

indicators.note: a bit of the egg is just its opening letter

parts.note: a gun is an arm, a weapon

explanation.surface: A pop gun firing egg causing a small injury, like a children's game gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes E from egg, and 'in' places it within DAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead arm is a temporary numbness from a blow to the upper arm, a playground injury.

clue.text: It measures radiation from reflective paste to frighten guards

indicators.note: guards means holds within, so the frighten word encloses the paste

parts.note: to frighten off is to deter

indicators.note: reflective means mirrored, so the paste word is read backwards

parts.note: miso is a Japanese fermented paste

explanation.surface: Some kind of mirrored paste deployed to scare off guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' turns the paste backwards, and 'guards' is a verb: the frighten word holds it. Miso is a Japanese soybean paste.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosimeter is a device recording exposure to ionising radiation.

clue.text: Queen forbidden to take clothes off

indicators.note: taking clothes off strips the outer layer, so the outer letters go

parts.note: forbidden means banned

explanation.surface: A queen barred from undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take clothes off' strips B and D from BANNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne was Queen of Great Britain in the early eighteenth century.

clue.text: Train A&E nurse to bind together

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold closely, so the outer pair holds the train word

parts.note: A&E stands for A and E, the two letters
a train is a string, a line of things one after another

explanation.surface: Training an emergency-department nurse to bandage things.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the hospital Accident and Emergency department; 'nurse' is a verb here, A and E holding STRING.
explanation.definitionFit: To astringe is to constrict or draw tissues tightly together.

clue.text: Disregard our current state

parts.note: to disregard is to miss out or overlook
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone advising us to ignore how things are now.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is a US state in the Midwest.

clue.text: Annoyed, avoided work away from sunshine, essentially

indicators.note: away from tells us to take letters out of the longer word

parts.note: to avoid work is to shirk, past tense shirked

indicators.note: essentially points to the core, the two central letters of sunshine

explanation.surface: Someone irritated after skiving work and staying out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives SH, the middle of sunshine, and 'away from' removes it from SHIRKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Irked is a synonym of annoyed or irritated.

clue.text: Salts found in pair of buttocks

parts.note: a pair of cheeks, the backside, is in British slang the arse
nates is the anatomical Latin term for the buttocks

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about finding salts somewhere on the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: ARSE is British slang for backside; NATES is the anatomical word for the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenates are chemical salts of arsenic acid.

clue.text: Taxing dumber ones works

indicators.note: works as a verb means to knead or rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather cruel remark that the less bright find work exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun or plain verb but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burdensome is onerous or demanding, as taxing work is.

clue.text: Hole on cover for pool

indicators.note: in an across answer, on puts the first piece after the second one

parts.note: a cover is a lid
O is a hole, from the shape of the letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for patching a pool cover with a hole in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: Break-in he'd orchestrated in part of Merseyside

indicators.note: orchestrated means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar boasting of a planned robbery near Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Merseyside is the county around Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Birkenhead is a town on the Wirral, across the Mersey from Liverpool.

clue.text: Rectify victory by German AfD candidate?

parts.note: to rectify is to put right
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: A German far-right politician hoping to correct things by winning.
explanation.walkthrough: AfD (Alternative für Deutschland) is a German far-right party; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate for that nationalist party would be a political conservative of the hard right.

clue.text: Holiday in Georgia ending in debauchery — that's a positive thing?

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of debauchery

parts.note: a cation is a positively charged ion

explanation.surface: A wild holiday in Georgia, questioned as a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'positive thing' is a cation, a positively charged ion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaycation is a holiday aimed at or taken by LGBT travellers.

clue.text: Overlook route for aircraft

parts.note: to overlook something is to skip it
a lane is a route or path

explanation.surface: Choosing which flight path to ignore.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiplane is an aeroplane fitted with skis to land on snow.

clue.text: Overweight visitor briefly hiding one's military overalls

parts.note: overweight means fat
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a visitor is a guest

explanation.surface: A heavy guest hiding someone's army gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the visitor's last letter, and 'hiding' tucks the one inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigues are soldiers' working clothes, a kind of military uniform.

clue.text: Returned kiss on vacation with Ray on Channel Island's major conurbation

indicators.note: returned means the whole string of pieces is read backwards
on vacation means the word kiss is emptied, leaving its outside letters

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France

explanation.surface: A holiday romance with someone called Ray on a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties kiss to KS; with RAYON and SARK the string KSRAYONSARK is 'Returned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Krasnoyarsk is a large Siberian city, a major urban centre in Russia.

clue.text: Mostly walking over Hollywood star

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: walking up and down is pacing
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A film star mostly seen walking about.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Pacino is a celebrated American film actor.

clue.text: Choose some Chinese lectures

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Picking which Chinese lectures to attend.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to pick or choose.

clue.text: Mate in tree, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear the word, judging it by sound

parts.note: a pear is a fruit tree

explanation.surface: Birds pairing up in a tree, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair is to mate or couple, as animals do.

clue.text: Work out the age of bubbly when daughter moves west

indicators.note: in an across answer, west is leftwards, so the letter shifts earlier in the word

parts.note: bubbly means fizzy, carbonated

explanation.surface: Seems to be about champagne and a daughter heading off west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne, but it is CARBONATED; shifting its D one place left gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiocarbon dating is used to establish how old organic remains are.

clue.text: Group eats in mid-morning to avoid Republican

indicators.note: to avoid means leave out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a late-morning meal is brunch

explanation.surface: A group eating mid-morning to keep clear of a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunch is a group or cluster of people or things.

clue.text: Exposed shoulder in audition

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so the sound counts

parts.note: to shoulder a load is to bear it

explanation.surface: An actor showing a shoulder at an audition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means uncovered or exposed.

clue.text: Made dull patios, one without any walls getting very high praise

indicators.note: without any walls means every word loses its outside letters

explanation.surface: A builder whose dull patios earned rapturous acclaim, even without walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulation is excessive admiration or flattery.

clue.text: English cricket team left watering-hole, ultimately getting banishment

parts.note: a cricket side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of watering-hole

explanation.surface: England's cricketers leaving the pub and being sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket team is called an eleven, written XI.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is enforced absence from one's country, a banishment.

clue.text: Records money sealing introduction to Eric Trump's close associate

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: sealing means enclosing, so the money word wraps round the letter

parts.note: tin is British slang for money

indicators.note: introduction to means the opening letter of Eric

explanation.surface: Seems to be about record sales and money involving Eric Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for cash. 'sealing' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeffrey Epstein was a well-known associate of Donald Trump.

clue.text: Enormous uncertainty picked up in retreat

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the sound of the words matters

parts.note: enormous means high, as in a high price; uncertainty is doubt

explanation.surface: Great doubts noticed during a withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a secluded refuge, a hiding place.
